task:
Refine the existing Stage 27A Spatial Platform proposal to make Elite Journal / Commander History and Elite Codex explicit cross-cutting product capabilities that integrate deeply with the Galaxy and System Maps while retaining their own non-map surfaces. IMPORTANT BASELINE: the accepted proposal-under-review currently lives on branch codex/run-33338816793-1 at commit d57b9be8e09da8bf68e2bc0a3f3c5cee3eadccf8, based on main commit a877afcb3b39c8e753b3f639b231d404c8be319b. This worker starts from current origin/main. Fetch the prior Codex branch/commit and apply that Stage 27A commit into the working tree WITHOUT committing (for example cherry-pick --no-commit) so the resulting implementation branch contains the complete original Stage 27A proposal plus this refinement. Do not silently drop any prior Stage27A files. If current main has moved and conflicts arise, preserve newer unrelated main changes while retaining the Stage27A intent. Do not commit/push yourself; wrapper owns that.

PRODUCT CORRECTION TO ADD:
1. The Journal must NOT be reduced to an Exploration ingestion implementation detail or raw event viewer. Establish it as a first-class ED-Finder Commander History / Journal capability. Inspiration is broadly EDSM-style commander history and statistics, but ED-Finder should be more interactive and spatial. Do not copy EDSM code/assets/UI. The Journal has its own page and remains useful without the map.
2. Journal page product purpose: meaningful commander history, statistics, filters, expeditions and records. Examples to explicitly support as future product requirements: total jumps; systems visited; distance travelled where derivable; ELWs found; Water Worlds; Ammonia Worlds; bodies scanned; bodies mapped; first discoveries/maps where the retained journal data supports the distinction; biological signals/finds; organic samples/sales; Codex observations; expeditions; regions visited; longest/farthest/chronological travel facts where the source permits. Raw events may be inspectable but are not the primary UX. Do not invent metrics that current Journal events cannot support; classify future/unknown inputs honestly.
3. Spatial projection rule: ANY Journal statistic, record, expedition or filtered result with meaningful spatial identity should be able to project onto the existing spatial platform through renderer-neutral SpatialContribution(s), rather than creating a separate Journal map. Example: Journal says '37 Earth-like worlds found' -> Show on Map -> highlight the 37 relevant systems; selecting one -> System Map highlights the actual ELW/body and shows personal discovery/scan/map context. '8,436 systems visited' -> show travel history. '2025 Beagle Point expedition' -> show/replay route. Codex observations -> show locations.
4. Reverse spatial query rule: the map can also ask Commander History questions. Examples: 'Summarise this area', 'Summarise selected systems', 'What did I discover here?', 'What did I miss?', 'show Journal facts within this viewport/selection/route'. Example area summary can include visited systems, ELWs, WWs, mapped bodies, biological finds and most recent visit, based only on available personal records.
5. Journal + Finder integration: make explicit that Journal-derived personal facts can become Finder predicates/filters without duplicating Finder or Journal logic. Examples: Earth-like worlds I have NOT discovered; Water Worlds near my 2025 expedition route that I never mapped; visited systems with incomplete scans; biological-signal bodies with no recorded completion. Finder remains query/ranking owner, Journal/Commander History remains personal-history owner, renderer only visualises results.
6. Journal as time dimension: Commander History should be capable of driving historical/timeline views. The platform should eventually support expedition playback and views such as 'show my personal record of this system at the time I visited it', ONLY where retained timestamped facts support that historical state. Never manufacture history or interpolate missing observations. Distinguish current catalogue knowledge from historical personal knowledge.
7. Journal data architecture: preserve immutable/raw source events where practical, then normalise/project them into product-ready commander history. Spatially meaningful observations should carry stable identity and scope: commander/account/sync key; timestamp; event identity/type; systemId64 where known; BodyRef {systemId64, bodyId} where known; source/provenance; structured payload; expedition/journey association where derived or user-assigned. Names may remain labels/fallback evidence, not canonical identity. Dedupe/idempotent import/replay should be a future implementation requirement.
8. Source separation: explicitly distinguish Elite Journal events from EDDN/public catalogue/CAPI data. Journal provides personal observations/history. Public/catalogue sources provide broader/current world knowledge. They may be compared but not silently merged into 'the commander discovered this'.
9. Codex distinction: keep two concepts separate: (a) game's broader Codex/catalogue knowledge where ED-Finder has an authoritative source; (b) the commander's personal CodexEntry observations captured via Journal. Personal Codex events belong in Commander History and can project spatially. Global/catalogue Codex knowledge must not be inferred from one commander's journal.
10. Three complementary surfaces to state explicitly: JOURNAL PAGE = statistics/history/records/filters/expeditions; GALAXY MAP = where those things happened; SYSTEM MAP = what exactly the commander did/discovered inside a system/body. These are views over shared underlying facts, not duplicated databases.
11. Add Journal/Commander History to the spatial feature inventory/capability audit and architecture stress tests. Preferred framing: Finder, Colonisation, Exploration/Journal, System Map, with Journal explicitly the commander-history backbone and Exploration one major interpretation/projection of it. Do not erase Exploration as a first-class user goal.
12. Stage sequencing: update Stage27 programme/docs so Journal integration is deliberately considered alongside spatial work. Do NOT opportunistically implement Journal ingestion/UI/runtime now. Stage27A remains contracts/audit only. Document which later stage(s) own: Journal data contract/import readiness; Journal page/analytics; Galaxy spatial contribution; System/body contribution; Finder integration; timeline/playback. You may refine Stage27F/27H responsibilities or add a clearly scoped later Journal substage if that produces a cleaner programme, but do not renumber/rewrite the entire programme casually. Stage27A must still authorize only 27B.
13. User-provided real logs: document as future optional validation/test data. Real commander logs can supplement synthetic deterministic fixtures for importer/replay/body identity/timestamps/exobio/Codex edge cases, but must be opt-in, privacy-safe/redacted where appropriate, never committed publicly without explicit approval, and never become the only test corpus. Synthetic fixtures remain required for deterministic regression tests.
14. EDSM reference: record EDSM/EDSM-NET only as product/research inspiration for commander-history/statistics and journal-event breadth, not as mechanics authority and not as a code/asset source. If external browsing is unavailable, do not make unverified detailed claims; ED-Finder's actual contracts should be based on Elite Journal event semantics and our own current repository evidence.

FILES TO REVIEW/UPDATE AT MINIMUM after restoring prior Stage27A proposal: docs/colonisation-redesign/spatial-platform-product-contract.md; docs/colonisation-redesign/spatial-platform-architecture-decision.md; docs/colonisation-redesign/stage-27a-spatial-capability-inventory.md; docs/colonisation-redesign/stage-27a-stage26-inheritance-matrix.md if Journal/exploration inheritance warrants it; docs/colonisation-redesign/stage-27a-system-map-data-readiness.md for Journal/body/Codex identity/readiness; docs/ROADMAP.md; CLAUDE.md; docs/colonisation-redesign/README.md; CHANGES.md. Update other Stage27A files only when materially needed. Preserve the old Babylon-plan superseded notice and stale-session-context correction from the prior branch.

CURRENT REPO EVIDENCE TO AUDIT, DO NOT JUST PARROT PROMPT: inspect existing exploration/journal import/facts/projections/APIs, including journal event models and support for FSDJump/CarrierJump/Location/Scan/FSSDiscoveryScan/FSSAllBodiesFound/SAASignalsFound/FSSBodySignals/CodexEntry/SAAScanComplete/ScanOrganic/SellOrganicData/SellExplorationData/MultiSellExplorationData/RedeemVoucher where current code actually supports them. Determine what current ED-Finder can already answer vs what needs later implementation. Preserve personal truth scope.

NO RUNTIME CHANGES: no Journal UI implementation, no importer activation, no Babylon implementation, no DB writes, no production access, no V2 changes, no deploy, no merge/main, no PR. Documentation/contracts/audit only. Run the repository state gate and proportional docs/hygiene/contract validation. End with a concise delta report: Journal/Commander History product contract added; current capability findings; later-stage ownership; privacy/test-data rule; files changed; validation; any genuine open decisions. Stop after corrected Stage27A proposal.
